summary: Markets face downward pressure as geopolitical tensions and inflation concerns weigh on sentiment. Oil prices pulled back to $90.12 after earlier spikes above $95 as U.S.-Iran hostilities continue, with the conflict costing taxpayers $37.5 billion and driving Treasury yields higher. Tech stocks extended losses with the Nasdaq down nearly 2% over the past month amid growing skepticism over AI spending returns. Tesla plunged 18% after Q2 operating profit missed forecasts by $1.3 billion, exemplifying earnings risk in high-profile growth names. Crypto markets weakened in tandem, with Bitcoin spot ETF outflows of $225 million breaking a weeklong positive streak as higher Treasury yields pulled capital from risk assets. Fed rate expectations have shifted, with markets now pricing 55% odds of a September hike and the forward curve pointing to the first 2026 rate cut delayed to July from earlier expectations.

signals.title: Tesla Q2 earnings miss by $1.3 billion triggers 18% crash
signals.desc: Tesla's Q2 operating profit shortfall highlights execution risk and valuation pressure across high-growth tech names as AI infrastructure spending fails to deliver near-term returns.

signals.title: Bitcoin ETF outflows hit $225 million, ending week-long streak
signals.desc: Rising Treasury yields and inflation fears drove institutional capital away from crypto as higher opportunity costs weigh on non-yielding assets like Bitcoin.

signals.title: Oil retreats 2.25% to $90 easing inflation pressures
signals.desc: WTI crude pulled back from highs above $95 despite ongoing Middle East hostilities, providing relief to equities sensitive to input costs and rate expectations.

signals.title: Fed September rate hike odds surge to 55% on oil, tariffs
signals.desc: Persistent inflation from oil supply disruptions and new global tariffs push Treasury yields higher and rate cut expectations further into 2026, pressuring equities and crypto.

signals.title: Alphabet cloud revenue beats expectations with $500B backlog
signals.desc: Google parent reported cloud revenue far surpassing estimates and disclosed massive contracted business backlog, offering selective support to AI infrastructure thesis amid broader tech selloff.

verdict: Defensive rotation continues as inflation and geopolitical risks trump AI optimism, favoring energy and commodities over tech and crypto.
